idiom_name: [InlineArray(N)] struct + Span<T> accessor, ArrayPool<T> for the spill
implementation_notes: [InlineArray] (C# 12 / .NET 8) is the language feature for this pattern: applied to a struct with a single field, 'the runtime replicates that field in the actual type layout as many times as is specified', so N elements live inside the object and can be exposed as a Span<T> without allocating an array. For payloads that outgrow the buffer, keep the spilled copy in a pooled array (ArrayPool<T>.Shared is 'a resource pool that enables reusing instances of type T[]') or in a normal heap collection; stackalloc gives stack-lifetime storage for a temporary span, so it complements the pattern but is not an in-object buffer. The classic union-plus-tag structure therefore has no C# counterpart - the runtime owns the type layout and the declaration site fixes the inline capacity up front - so pick that capacity conservatively and treat the pooled array as the general spill path. Note the .NET 9 behaviour change: the default Equals()/GetHashCode() implementations of inline-array types throw NotSupportedException, so override both or keep the type internal.
pitfalls: In .NET 9 and later the default Equals()/GetHashCode() for a type marked [InlineArray] throw NotSupportedException - override both if the struct is ever compared, boxed into a dictionary or used with records.

An inline array is not an array: it has no Length property, only becomes a Span<T>/ReadOnlySpan<T> through conversion, and any boxing (object, IEnumerable, non-generic APIs) copies or allocates, which defeats the optimization.

The buffer is part of the struct, so every copy memcpys the whole inline array; passing it by value through a call chain can cost more than the array allocation it avoids - access it through ref/Span and keep it out of large value-type wrappers.
sources: Microsoft Learn, System.Runtime.CompilerServices.InlineArrayAttribute - 'Indicates that the instance's storage is sequentially replicated Length times ... the runtime replicates that field in the actual type layout as many times as is specified', plus the .NET 9 Equals/GetHashCode note: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.runtime.compilerservices.inlinearrayattribute
Microsoft Learn, System.Buffers.ArrayPool<T> - 'Provides a resource pool that enables reusing instances of type T[]': https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.buffers.arraypool-1
